subject: convergence problems in multigroup model with categorial indicators

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: convergence problems in multigroup model with categorial indicators
parts:
Hi,

i set up a multigroup model with categorial indicators, following the advice at http://people.ku.edu/~s044p855/catInvariance.html

however, the model fails to convergate and i get some high variances, loadings and thresholds. i suspect that this results from my sample size beeing too small (n = 500 for a unidimensional model with 9 indicators and 4 categories), too sparse categories or that in both groups there is a considerable mean difference in the factor.

are there any strategies to find out where the problems are? are there strategies to sort these problems out, eg by collapsing categories?

my model looks like this:

Overall =~ c(1, 1)*item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_4 + item_5 + item_6 + item_7 + item_8 + item_9

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: convergence problems in multigroup model with categorial indicators
parts:
This is an interesting example. My guess would be that you have many
'empty' cells in your pairwise tables in group 2. What happens if you
add the argument:

zero.add=c(0.5, 0.5)

to the cfa/sem call? It is the second value that is used, since you have
more than 2 response categories. If it helps, try to lower the value
until you get trouble.

If this doesn't help: could you send me your data (I would only need
group 2 data) and R script?

Yves.
